accepted.s: The title ‘Maharshi’ is associated with which of the following leaders of the Andhra freedom movement?
accepted.x: Bulusu Sambamurthy was popularly known as ‘Maharshi’ because of his ascetic Gandhian way of life.
accepted.tq: Use direct title–person recall while distinguishing similar honorifics.
accepted.sec: Leaders' popular titles → person + episode behind the title

accepted.s: Who among the following was known as ‘Andhra Ratna’?
accepted.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was called ‘Andhra Ratna’. He led the Chirala-Perala Satyagraha in 1921 and founded the Ramadandu volunteer corps.
accepted.tq: Match the popular title with the leader and the associated movement.
accepted.sec: Leaders' popular titles → person + episode behind the title

accepted.s: ‘Desoddharaka’ was the title associated with which of the following personalities?
accepted.x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was known as ‘Desoddharaka’ and was the founder of Andhra Patrika.
accepted.tq: Apply confusable-title discrimination among prominent Andhra leaders.
accepted.sec: Leaders' popular titles → person + episode behind the title

accepted.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was popularly known as ‘Andhra Tilak’ mainly because of his:
o: courage during the Vande Mataram era
accepted.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao earned the title ‘Andhra Tilak’ for his courage during the Vande Mataram era.
accepted.tq: Identify the episode or quality behind a title rather than merely recalling the name.
accepted.sec: Leaders' popular titles → person + episode behind the title

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao — Ramadandu volunteer corps
accepted.x: Bulusu Sambamurthy was associated with an ascetic Gandhian life. Andhra Patrika was founded by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, the Ramadandu was founded by Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya, and the Chirala-Perala Satyagraha was led by him.
accepted.tq: Find the sure person–episode pair and eliminate swapped associations.
accepted.sec: Leaders' popular titles → person + episode behind the title

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about posts held by Pattabhi Sitaramayya:
1. He was Governor of Madhya Pradesh from 1952 to 1957.
2. He was a member of the Rajya Sabha.
3. He served as President of the Indian National Congress at Jaipur in 1948.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya held all three positions: Governor of Madhya Pradesh during 1952–1957, Rajya Sabha member, and INC President at Jaipur in 1948.
accepted.tq: Test a cluster of offices held by one leader using an all-statements option.
accepted.sec: Posts held → leader

accepted.s: Who served as President of the Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee in 1937?
accepted.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya served as President of the Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee in 1937.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an organisational post from the leader’s other national offices.
accepted.sec: Posts held → leader

accepted.s: Tanguturi Prakasam held which of the following offices in the Rajaji Ministry of 1937?
accepted.x: Tanguturi Prakasam served as Revenue Minister in the Rajaji Ministry of 1937.
accepted.tq: Use the ministry-and-portfolio association to avoid swapping offices.
accepted.sec: Posts held → leader

accepted.s: Tanguturi Prakasam became the Chief Minister or Premier of composite Madras in:
accepted.x: Tanguturi Prakasam became Chief Minister, then referred to as Premier, of composite Madras in 1946.
accepted.tq: Use a year-based distinction between Prakasam’s Madras and Andhra offices.
accepted.sec: Posts held → leader

accepted.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding Tanguturi Prakasam’s later public career?
o: He was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State in 1953.
He was President of the INC at Jaipur in 1948.
He was the second and last Chief Minister of Andhra State.
He served as Governor of Madhya Pradesh from 1952 to 1957.
accepted.x: Tanguturi Prakasam became the first Chief Minister of Andhra State in 1953. Bezawada Gopal Reddy was the second and last Chief Minister of Andhra State.
accepted.tq: Separate closely related Andhra State chief ministerships.
accepted.sec: Posts held → leader

accepted.s: Tanguturi Prakasam was elected President of the Andhra Congress Committee how many times?
accepted.x: Tanguturi Prakasam was elected President of the Andhra Congress Committee 18 times.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive numerical figure using nearby but incorrect counts as distractors.
accepted.sec: Posts held → leader

accepted.s: Who was the second and last Chief Minister of Andhra State, serving from 28 March 1955 to 31 October 1956?
accepted.x: Bezawada Gopal Reddy was the second and last Chief Minister of Andhra State, holding office from 28 March 1955 to 31 October 1956.
accepted.tq: Use dates to distinguish successive holders of the same office.
accepted.sec: Posts held → leader

Study of national flags — Patti Venkayya

accepted.s: Which one of the following books was written by Pattabhi Sitaramayya?
accepted.x: ‘Feathers and Stones’, described as an Ahmednagar Fort prison diary, was written by Pattabhi Sitaramayya.
accepted.tq: Distinguish authorship by separating books of Pattabhi, Prakasam and Konda Venkatappayya.

accepted.s: Which of the following works was written by Tanguturi Prakasam?
o: History of the Indian National Congress

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. ‘Naa Jeevita Yatra’ is the autobiography of Tanguturi Prakasam.
2. The autobiography consists of four parts.
3. Tanguturi Prakasam wrote all four parts himself.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: ‘Naa Jeevita Yatra’ is Prakasam’s autobiography and consists of four parts. However, Prakasam wrote three parts, while Tenneti Viswanatham wrote the fourth.
accepted.tq: Spot the subtle false statement created by an absolute claim such as ‘all’.
accepted.sec: Books written → author

accepted.s: Which of the following works is NOT associated with Tanguturi Prakasam?
accepted.x: ‘Andhrudyamam’ was written by Konda Venkatappayya. Law Times, Monetary Systems of the World and Indian Monetary Systems were associated with Tanguturi Prakasam.
accepted.tq: Find the one work belonging to a different author in a grouped list.
accepted.sec: Books written → author

accepted.s: Pattabhi Sitaramayya wrote articles in The Hindu on the need for:
accepted.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya wrote articles in The Hindu advocating the need for linguistic states.
accepted.tq: Identify the subject of a leader’s published advocacy.
accepted.sec: Books written → author

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events connected with Konda Venkatappayya in chronological order:
A. Presidency of the fifth Andhra Mahasabha session at Nellore
B. Presidency of the Swadeshi meeting at Tenali
C. Secretaryship of the Nidadavolu standing committee
D. Secretaryship of the first Andhra Mahasabha session at Bapatla
accepted.x: The correct order is Tenali Swadeshi meeting (1907), Nidadavolu standing committee (1912), Bapatla session (1913), and Nellore session (1917).
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last events, then arrange the middle events by year.

accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of the first session from the years of related Andhra organisations.

He was a lawyer who gave up his legal practice.
